Personality in motion: body language and the Big Five

personality big five meta-analysis web apps data visualization

An interactive field guide to the facial, body and voice cues that a meta-analysis of 65 studies links to the Big Five traits - and to how small those links are.

Luděk Stehlík https://www.linkedin.com/in/ludekstehlik/
2026-11-22

Recently, I came across an interesting piece of research via a Minerva Psychology post about how personality is linked to body language, and how well people’s intuitive theories match the empirical findings in this area.

The study (Hall et al., 2025) asked 245 US adults how likely 20 nonverbal behaviours are for someone high in one of the Big Five traits, and compared their answers with a meta-analysis of 65 studies on how people actually behave (Breil et al., 2021). For four of the five traits, people’s beliefs matched the evidence fairly well. Openness was the exception.

When reading the paper, I thought that, given the subject of the study, it could be cool to give the main findings a more concrete and interactive form than boring charts and tables. So I built a small app where you pick a trait and an animated figure plays out the facial, body and voice cues that showed a clear link to it in the meta-analysis. (OK, one chart stayed, so you can also see how strong each link is 🙂)

Check it out here 👉 Personality in motion

Maybe you’ll find it useful when training body language for a specific persona 🙃

⚠️ Just keep in mind that all 21 links are small, so a single cue tells you very little about any one person.
